title: S3 adapter: add SSE-KMS support + cross-account assume-role credentials (docs + IAM snippets)
author: Hanae Suzuki
release_notes: S3 audit export destinations can now (1) encrypt objects using SSE-KMS with a customer-provided KMS key and (2) deliver to cross-account buckets by assuming a customer-provided IAM role (optional external ID).
description: Summary: This extends the S3 destination adapter to support SSE-KMS (SSE with customer-managed keys) and an assume-role credential flow for cross-account bucket delivery. It also adds operator-facing documentation with minimal IAM policy snippets (bucket policy, role trust policy, and KMS key policy guidance) that we can share with beta customers. Motivation: During early beta onboarding we hit two recurring enterprise requirements: (1) buckets enforced with "s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption" conditions (must be aws:kms) and (2) cross-account delivery where the customer does not want to place a static access key in Redwood; instead they provide an IAM Role ARN that Redwood assumes (with optional ExternalId). This PR implements both requirements while keeping least-privilege defaults and avoiding secret leakage in logs. Design/behavior: - New S3 destination fields (config schema + validation): sse (enum: "SSE-S3" | "SSE-KMS"), kms_key_arn (required when sse=="SSE-KMS"), role_arn (optional), external_id (optional but recommended when role_arn is set), session_name (optional; defaults to "redwood-audit-exporter"). - When role_arn is provided, the adapter uses STS AssumeRole to obtain credentials; credentials are cached with the AWS SDK provider cache (we rely on SDK refresh semantics; exporter does not persist temp creds). - When sse=="SSE-KMS", PutObject / multipart uploads include ServerSideEncryption=aws:kms and SSEKMSKeyId=<kms_key_arn>. When SSE-S3, we omit the headers entirely (customers can enforce bucket default encryption or use SSE-S3 conditions). - Multipart upload path: CreateMultipartUpload now sets the encryption headers so that completed objects remain encrypted; this was previously a footgun when customers enforced KMS-only. - Logging: we log role_arn at INFO only during destination init, but do not log external_id, do not log any credential source chain, and we redact kms_key_arn to the key ID suffix in debug logs (full ARN can be considered sensitive in some customer environments). IAM docs added: docs/s3-cross-account-and-kms.md includes a copy/paste starter set for: - Customer account: Role trust policy allowing Redwood AWS account to assume role with optional ExternalId condition (StringEquals). - Permissions policy on the role to allow s3:PutObject, s3:AbortMultipartUpload, s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads, s3:ListBucket, s3:ListMultipartUploadParts scoped to the bucket/prefix. - Bucket policy condition examples: requiring aws:kms and requiring a specific KMS key ARN, plus allowing the assumed role principal. - KMS key policy guidance: allow the assumed role to use kms:Encrypt/kms:GenerateDataKey for the key, scoped via encryption context and/or via s3 service principal condition (kms:ViaService == s3.<region>.amazonaws.com). Notes: This PR intentionally does not add support for customer-provided STS endpoints / GovCloud partitions; we’ll cover that in follow-on once we finalize region partitioning for dedicated tenants. Testing: - Unit tests: (1) validation rejects SSE-KMS without kms_key_arn; (2) assume-role provider is wired when role_arn set; (3) multipart upload requests include the right SSE headers. - Integration harness: localstack-based smoke tests updated to assert x-amz-server-side-encryption headers; a cross-account assume-role test uses two localstack accounts (best-effort; skipped in CI if localstack does not support multi-account assume role in the pinned image). Rollout: Feature-flagged via existing destination config; safe to merge without enabling for customers. Docs can be shared immediately with CS/SE for onboarding. References: - ENG-5144 (S3 destination adapter w/ checkpointing) - ENG-5189 (threat model: secrets, egress, least privilege) - PR-1061 (initial S3 adapter) - PR-1105 (destination validation / egress allowlist follow-up; not required for this change but complementary).

conversation: Diego Santos (review): For SSE-KMS on multipart, are we setting encryption on CreateMultipartUpload or on individual parts? (If only on parts, the final object may fail policy enforcement.)
Hanae Suzuki (author): Good catch — updated to set SSE headers on CreateMultipartUpload as well. Added unit coverage that asserts the request fields on create + complete path.
Marcus Lin (security): Please make sure we don’t log external_id and that role session names are stable (helps customers audit STS events). Also add doc guidance that ExternalId is recommended.

Hanae Suzuki (author): Done. external_id is never logged; session_name defaults to "redwood-audit-exporter" (overrideable). Docs updated with ExternalId recommendation + example trust policy condition.
Kevin Osei (security): Can we include a minimal KMS key policy snippet? Customers always ask, and missing kms:GenerateDataKey causes confusing failures.
Hanae Suzuki (author): Added a “common failure modes” section and a minimal key policy example (Encrypt/GenerateDataKey) with notes on scoping using kms:ViaService and bucket prefix restrictions.
Sean Gallagher (SRE): Any risk of thundering herd on STS if the exporter restarts across many tenants?

Hanae Suzuki (author): Using the SDK’s credential cache; sessions are per-destination and refresh ahead of expiry. Worst case on restart is one AssumeRole per configured S3 destination; we can add jittered warm-up later if needed.
Diego Santos (review): Please add explicit validation to fail fast when sse==SSE-KMS and kms_key_arn is empty; otherwise customers get opaque AccessDenied from S3/KMS.
Hanae Suzuki (author): Added validation + surfaced a friendly error in destination status: "SSE-KMS requires kms_key_arn".
Marcus Lin (approval): LGTM after the logging redaction and doc updates.
Sean Gallagher (approval): LGTM; thanks for calling out the localstack limitation in CI output.
